title: Marvel's "Dumbest" Mutant Power Is Real — Starfish Do It Every Day
youtube_description:
Marvel's most mocked mutant power is just ordinary starfish biology.

In 1997, Uncanny X-Men #345 introduced Maggott: a mutant with a hollow gut and two giant slugs living inside it, named Eany and Meany. The slugs crawl out, eat through almost anything (metal, stone, flesh), crawl back in and turn that meal into raw superhuman strength. Fans called him the worst X-Man ever made.

Except nature already built him. A starfish doesn't swallow its food. It pushes its stomach out through its own mouth and digests its prey alive, outside its body. To get into a sealed clam, that stomach squeezes through a gap under a millimetre wide, narrower than the edge of a coin. It floods the clam with enzymes, digests it from the inside out, then pulls the stomach back in.

The joke didn't age well either. In Storm #6 (March 2025), Marvel made Maggott an Omega-level mutant, one of the most powerful beings in the Marvel universe. So the dumbest mutant power ever written turned out to be real biology, and it's happening in every tide pool on Earth.

This channel digs up the real science and buried history behind Marvel's strangest characters. Subscribe for more of them.

Sources: Wikipedia (Maggott); CBR ("The Last Mutant You'd Expect Just Got Omega-Level Powers"); Screen Rant ("After 28 Years, X-Men Unleashes the Full Power of Its Most Underrated Omega Mutant"); starfish feeding and stomach eversion: ochre sea star (Pisaster ochraceus) feeding studies.
